On the precision class, f_A(x)=xᵀAx/2, π_A=N(0,A^(−1)), FO_A(x)=(xᵀAx/2, Ax).

nodes.claim_or_meaning: The spectrum is deterministic and may be known to the algorithm; the normalizing constant is known; the unknown component is the eigenbasis.
For every O∈O(d), A=OΛOᵀ satisfies I_d ≼ A ≼ κ I_d.
nodes.notes: This is the literal numbered conclusion, under the family assumptions d≥2, κ≥2. It is not a claim about all arbitrary matrices or all arbitrary fixed spectra.

nodes.notes: V_A is a notational rename of f_A, not a second potential formula.

nodes.claim_or_meaning: The potential is 1-strongly convex and κ-smooth.
V_A(0)=0 and V_A(x)≥||x||²/2>0 for x≠0; the origin is the unique minimizer.
The associated target is N(0,A^(−1)).
Gaussian integration gives Z_A=(2π)^(d/2)(det A)^(−1/2).
det(OΛOᵀ)=det Λ, hence Z_A=(2π)^(d/2)(det Λ)^(−1/2).
Because Λ is fixed, Z_A is independent of O and is known whenever the spectrum is public.
Theorem 4.1: for fixed δ∈(0,1), d≥d0(δ), 2≤κ≤d^(1−δ), 0<ε≤1/10, Q_G≥(δ/256)√κ log d; the family can have a public spectrum.
nodes.notes: The lower-bound proof is not claimed from admissibility alone. Its distinct Krylov/moment/test arguments are excluded from this bounded target closure.
